text:
A year ago Juuse Saros allowed 10.2 more goals than his shots deserved over 59 games, and Nashville's season went with him. This fall he has flipped it: 9.9 goals saved above expected (the goals he has kept out beyond what an average goalie would, given the shots), 83rd percentile, with a .918 save percentage. Yahoo Sports already has him at the top of its Vezina rankings.

The stretch that made it was early November, when the Predators reeled off seven straight wins and Saros posted a 3-0 shutout in Los Angeles. He saved more than expected in four straight starts through Nov. 13. San Jose ended the streak, and on Tuesday in Minnesota he came on in relief after Justus Annunen allowed six goals on 20 shots, giving up one the rest of the way.

Our talent range keeps his true save rate a little below his current .918, so some of this will settle. His low-danger work (.981 against a league .963) is the steadiest piece. For a goalie with a 7-4-4 record, he has been the margin more nights than not. Watch whether he gets the next start straight back.
headline: Saros is back to stealing games
